harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed the app on node2 and published it through node1 (a VyOS gateway) to node3 using Ansible run from node4 (the control_node), while keeping the rest of the node1/node2 private network closed off to node3. Verified functionality and persistence across a one-at-a-time restart of all four managed nodes.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS gateway (10.100.61.10), node2=app host (10.100.61.11, Ubuntu), node3=external client (10.100.61.12), node4=Ansible control_node (10.100.61.13); all four sit on one flat /24 with node2's default route pointing to the platform gateway, not node1.

Bootstrapped SSH management access: created an antrieb sudo user + authorized_keys on node2/node3, and used VyOS's native 'set system login user antrieb ...' config on node1 so it persists reboots; fixed missing SSH host keys on node2/node3.

Wrote /root/publish-app.yml (Ansible playbook, 3 plays): (1) install nginx on node2 serving the app on :8080, lock down with ufw so only node1 may reach :8080 and node3 is denied everything except via node1; (2) configure VyOS on node1 with destination NAT (8080->node2:8080) + hairpin source NAT (masquerade, required because node2's default gateway isn't node1) + default-drop forward filter permitting only the published flow; (3) verification play from node3 confirming reachability via node1 and refusal directly via node2.

Ran the playbook via node4's run.sh (EXECUTED_FILE mechanism) against an inventory.ini I created; worked around a bash alias-expansion pitfall in the VyOS configure block by writing a real script file instead of `bash -c '...'`.
Found and fixed a stale broad allow-22-from-anywhere ufw rule left by an earlier partial run by adding an explicit delete task; verified idempotent re-run cleaned it up.
Captured healthy baselines (boot_id, live VyOS NAT/firewall show output, nginx/ufw active state, app response) on all four nodes.

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot, polling each until exec access returned, proving a changed boot_id each time, and re-verifying NAT/firewall config, app reachability, and access restrictions after each restart.

After node1's restart, discovered VyOS resets non-VyOS-managed Linux users on boot (the raw useradd antrieb account vanished); fixed by re-adding the user through VyOS's own config system, which persisted through a later re-run.
Re-ran the playbook from node4 after all four restarts to confirm full idempotent recovery end-to-end, and did a final manual verification from node3.

evidence.requirement: App published through node1 on port 8080, reachable from node3
evidence.summary: Ansible verification play and direct curl from node3 to http://10.100.61.10:8080/ return 'app on node2 (via node1 gateway)'

evidence.requirement: Rest of the private network NOT opened to node3 (no direct app or SSH access to node2)
evidence.summary: Direct curl from node3 to node2:8080 times out (connection dropped by ufw+VyOS default-drop forward filter); direct SSH (22) from node3 to node2 also times out after the ufw hardening task, both before and after all four node restarts

evidence.requirement: Implemented using Ansible, run from the configured control_node (node4)
evidence.summary: /root/publish-app.yml executed via node4's run.sh (ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini) against node1/node2/node3, using only ansible-core + community.general modules already present on node4

evidence.requirement: VyOS NAT/firewall configuration correctly published and default-drop for everything else
evidence.summary: show nat destination/source rules and show firewall confirm DNAT 8080->10.100.61.11:8080, hairpin masquerade SNAT, and forward filter default-action drop with only the 8080 flow (plus established/related) accepted

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 01735c83...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 76086c9d... (uptime 23.6s); NAT/firewall config intact and app reachable via node1 again

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 1e0cb179...; reboot issued; post-restart boot_id 590f2fd6... (uptime 3.76s); nginx active, ufw rules intact, app serving locally and via node1, still blocked directly from node3

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 901ef286...; reboot issued; post-restart boot_id 5b4ff0b9... (uptime 4.06s); node3 can still reach the app via node1 and is still blocked from node2 directly

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d5f5239f...; reboot issued; post-restart boot_id c2161638... (uptime 3.87s); ansible-playbook tooling and inventory/playbook files intact, full playbook re-run against node1/node2/node3 succeeded
